audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the full-layer chart disagreed with the content layer: full read Xerath/Xerath/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill against content and packet Skill/Skill/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath.
audit.why: Xerath is mana-starved with one rank of Arcanopulse at level 1 and your Q reaches 900 to his 750, so the first two levels are genuinely even; from level 3 his 1000-range W and 1050-range E out-distance everything you own and never give it back.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides moved onto the content layer, ratings aligned, and every why rewritten to match its new verdict.

audit.why: Xerath spikes at Manaflow completion (his passive plus mana items fix his only weakness), at 6 with Rite of the Arcane's 5000-range barrage on a 130s cooldown, and at each item as poke cost stops mattering. Yours are Lost Chapter, 6, and Liandry's.

audit.whatIsWrong: The one interaction that decides the matchup was never stated: Shocking Orb is hard CC and Nether Grasp is an interruptible channel, so his E is the single button that stops your ultimate — and Void Shift's crowd control immunity is what beats it. The packet also flagged zero sequencing cues anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Kit flags: enemy E hardCC, owner R channel (interruptible — any CC cancels it), owner passive grants crowd control immunity while up.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field now carries Shocking Orb 13s->11s, Arcanopulse 9s->5s and the Void Shift interaction; dos/donts now key off that cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and packet.defects reported no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Shocking Orb barely scales — 13s at rank 1 and still 11s at rank 5 — which is precisely why the downtime is exploitable and worth printing.
audit.corrected: Numbers added and the step-up keyed to them.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim; report[7].t made an unsourced 'doubles' claim.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten grounded in Xerath's ranges and cooldowns.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget spell shield (Iron Boundary) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1 and still 11s maxed — his only CC, and the only thing that cancels Nether Grasp, so step up on its downtime. - Arcanopulse is 9s at rank 1, 5s maxed. - Void Shift is CC immunity: a full shield eats the orb.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Xerath wins by out-ranging you at 1050, stunning you out of Nether Grasp, and chipping you off CS from total safety.

edits.before: Carry by subtraction — every fight starts 4v5 when your R lands; your job is the wave control that makes the fight happen on your timer.
edits.after: Carry from the fog — Nether Grasp on Xerath ends him outright, so flank past his 1050-range stun instead of walking at him down the lane.

edits.before: You are a suppression delivery system: shield up, hold a flank, and Grasp their carry the moment the fight breathes. The visions and burn do the rest.
edits.after: Hold a flank with Zhonya and Void Shift charged. Shocking Orb is the only thing that stops the channel, so make him spend it before you appear.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Voidlings and visions clear from 650 while he pokes from 1000 — crash the wave, take the reset, and spend the tempo on a roam rather than a trade.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: With Void Shift down, one Shocking Orb at 1050 range turns his whole barrage into a kill — walk up only with the shield charged.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport standard — TP doubles your shove-tax map game. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport standard — TP turns every crashed wave into a map play. Cleanse answers the Shocking Orb stun that cancels your R; Ignite pairs with R kill threats.

edits.after: Shocking Orb every 13s plus Rite of the Arcane at 5000 range give him stun-and-artillery poke from outside your 700 R; the orb also cancels your channel outright unless Void Shift is up, so stepping up under his barrage is where he wins the lane.

edits.before: He keeps the advantage at two-plus items. A farmed Xerath is artillery incarnate, and your stationary channel makes you his dream target from max range. Your only real threat is a flank: Zhonya up, walk the fog, and land a full E-W-Q into R suppress before he can Shocking Orb you. Otherwise, farm side lanes safely, let your team engage past his poke, and rely on picks rather than a straight lane win.

notes: The full-layer chart disagreed with the content layer on all seven rows; both now read Skill/Skill/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath, matching packet.levelChart. Packet flagged zero sequencing cues in this matchup; the cooldowns field, dos/donts, spikes[1] and late now key advice to Shocking Orb's 13s-to-11s cooldown.
